action_items.text: Review the minutes that were emailed and placed in the shared folder.
Make a decision on the remote control functions.
Design several different prototypes of user interfaces for the product and gather feedback on how well they work.
Design a remote control that is simple, easy to use, has big buttons for frequent tasks (volume/channel), looks cool, and is ergonomically designed.
Work on the chip that converts electrical energy into data for the infra-red signal.
Find a long-lasting energy source that does not require frequent battery changes.
Design a chip that works well with the user interface and is not too complicated.
Design a straightforward user interface that is simple and not overwhelming.
Ensure a reliable and clear infra-red signal so users do not have to wave the remote around excessively.
Complete a questionnaire and a summary.
Put up the minutes and project documentation, including PowerPoint slides.
Note any frustrations or issues that come up in the summary.

decisions.text: The group will proceed with the presentations in the order they were originally listed.
The team will not include teletext functionality in the new remote control design because it has been taken over by the internet.
Management has decided not to work with the old Ceefax-style technology.
The project will focus on 'Just for television' rather than video or other formats to keep it simple and quick.
The corporate image must be recognizable, using the company's yellow, black, and 'fashion in electronics' slogan.
Voice recognition will not be included as a function because it adds too much to the price and is not necessary for a remote control.
The target group is defined by income and ownership of a television rather than specific age demographics.
The remote must include a function to keep it from getting lost (e.g., a button to make it ring/beep).
The remote must have large, accessible buttons for essential functions.
The remote must have a possibility to access extra functions that are hidden or less prominent than main features.
The remote must be fashionable so it is not an eyesore on a coffee table.
The team should investigate whether the remote needs a battery or if it could use a rechargeable battery/charging station instead.
